comparison: Perfect agreement on phylogenetic identification of the GIC clade (C56, C57, C105, C108). Both evaluations find the phylogenetic analysis well-supported and compelling, with no challenges to these claims.

Partial disagreement on mitochondrial localization claims (C60-C62 vs C61-C62, C113-C114). OpenEval finds immunoconfocal data sufficient for mitochondrial localization. Peer reviewers accept mitochondrial localization but request additional protease protection experiments to confirm inner membrane topology, rating evidence as UNCERTAIN without this confirmation.

Agreement on thermostability data (C63-C66 overlap with C65-C66, C77-C80). Both evaluations accept nanoDSF and thermostability shift assays as valid evidence for substrate binding, with peer reviewers specifically noting this methodology is convincing.

OpenEval addresses comprehensive thermostability binding profiles (C71-C82), while peer R3 focuses on subset (C65-C66, C77-C80). Both accept thermostability methodology as valid for demonstrating substrate binding, though OpenEval notes it doesn't prove transport activity.

Agreement on bGIC-2 transport data for negative controls and inorganic ions (C83-C88). Both evaluations accept the transport assay data showing no uptake for certain substrates by bGIC-1 and positive transport of phosphate/sulphate by bGIC-2.

Agreement on bGIC-2 transport of phosphate and sulphate (C86-C88). Both evaluations accept this transport data as demonstrating functionality, with peer reviewers calling it 'solid and well-executed.'

Agreement on control carrier characterization (C89-C92 overlap with C89-C90, C92). Both evaluations accept the substrate profiles for reference carriers, though OpenEval notes pyruvate explanation is speculative.

Agreement on DHAP transport and control experiments (C93-C96 overlap with C93-C94, C97-C98). Both accept the characterization of reference carriers, with peer reviewers noting hDIC binding to glycolytic intermediates as valid data.
Agreement on bOGC characterization (C97-C98, C111-C112 overlap with C97-C98). Both evaluations accept bOGC as a functional homologue of human carriers with appropriate substrate specificity.

Partial overlap on comparative substrate specificity (C97-C98, C111-C112 vs C5, C99-C100, C111-C112). Both accept the comparative data, though peer reviewers note concern about under-emphasizing that hDIC also binds glycolytic intermediates.

Strong agreement on key finding of glycolytic intermediate transport by bGIC-2 (C99-C101, C117 overlap with C47, C101, C117, C125). Both evaluations identify this as the central 'missing link' finding, though peer reviewers note lack of in vivo confirmation as a caveat.

Agreement on bGIC-2 transport of glycolytic intermediates (C99-C101, C117 overlap with C5, C99-C100, C111-C112). Both accept the transport data showing bGIC-2's novel substrate specificity and loss of canonical substrate transport.

Significant disagreement on central conclusion (C4, C47-C48, C103-C104, C146 overlap with C4, C48, C103-C104, C146). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on convergent evidence. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN due to lack of in vivo validation, stating evidence is 'convincing, albeit lacking direct in vivo confirmation of the physiological function.'

Partial overlap on central finding (C4, C47-C48, C103-C104, C146 vs C47, C101, C117, C125). OpenEval finds convergent evidence strongly supports the conclusion. Peer reviewers accept the in vitro transport data but note lack of in vivo confirmation limits confidence in physiological function.

Agreement on functional divergence (C5, C84 overlap with C5, C99-C100, C111-C112). Both evaluations accept that bGIC-2 has lost canonical substrate transport, representing functional divergence from ancestral carrier function.
Minimal overlap on negative transport results (C5, C84 vs C83-C88). Both accept the negative transport data for certain substrates, with OpenEval noting this represents functional divergence.

Agreement on mitochondrial localization but different emphasis (C113-C115 overlap with C61-C62, C113-C114). OpenEval accepts localization and notes speculation about substrate identity. Peer reviewers accept localization but request membrane topology confirmation.

Perfect agreement on compensatory mechanisms (C119-C122). Both evaluations accept the phylogenetic analysis showing reduced carrier complement and the inference about bGIC-2 compensating for absent DIC homologue.

Agreement on metabolic pathway model (C124-C127 overlap with C126-C127, C129, C142). Both evaluations accept the metabolic inferences about PEP as counter-solute, with peer reviewers requesting better presentation in Figure 7 but confirming the logic is sound.

Minimal overlap on DHAP transport (C124-C127 vs C47, C101, C117, C125). Both accept C125 regarding DHAP transport, with OpenEval noting the broader metabolic pathway is a model rather than directly demonstrated flux.

Partial overlap on metabolic inferences (C128-C129, C131 vs C126-C127, C129, C142). Both evaluations accept the genomic data and metabolic inferences connecting DHAP transport to Blastocystis metabolism.
Minimal overlap on genomic context (C128-C129, C131 vs C136-C141). Both evaluations accept genomic data about Blastocystis as established context supporting the metabolic rationale.

Perfect agreement on metabolic context (C136-C141). Both evaluations accept the genomic data and metabolic inferences about Blastocystis's compartmentalized glycolysis as established context not challenged by reviewers.

Agreement on uncertainty of therapeutic claims (C9, C50, C147). Both rate as UNCERTAIN/speculative. OpenEval notes no drug development studies presented. Peer reviewers raise concern that mitochondrial TPI may obviate need for these carriers as drug targets, undermining the therapeutic potential claim.

OpenEval finds general conclusions about branched glycolysis and novel substrate specificity (C144-C145) are SUPPORTED by overall findings. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found, though these conclusions align with peer acceptance of the underlying data.

OpenEval finds background context claims (C3, C14, C28-C29, C49, C51-C52) are SUPPORTED by citations to prior work. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found, though peer R12 acknowledges this context as established.
